title: Why 24 FPS Looks Smooth in Movies but Choppy in Games
description:
Movies run at 24 frames a second and look smooth. A game at 24 looks choppy. A film camera's shutter stays open for half of each frame, so moving things are smeared and your brain blends the smears into motion. A game draws every frame perfectly sharp, so you see the jumps. At 60 fps each jump is less than half as big, and because you're steering, a new frame every 42 milliseconds also feels late.

Sources:
- ARRI / American Cinematographer Manual: 180-degree shutter rule, exposure time = 1/(2 x frame rate).
- UC Berkeley CS184 (2023), lecture 17 'Intro to animation': motion blur and temporal sampling in rendered vs filmed frames.
- Game Developer, 'Framerate and refresh: games and movies are not the same' (motion blur in film vs games).

How it's made: original 3D characters and scenes, animated by us. The voices are AI voices (ElevenLabs).

Counterphysical: gaming science that breaks your intuition.
